watchlist.thesis: Post-earnings momentum is supported by 13% backlog growth, record fourth-quarter margins and 104% free-cash-flow growth; strong turnover confirms participation, while lower reported revenue and project-execution risk favor pullback entries over chasing.

A fresh post-earnings continuation setup is backed by 33% fourth-quarter revenue growth, 59% EPS growth, 162% quarterly order growth and a 96% backlog increase; liquidity is strong, with order conversion and project concentration the main risks.

Post-results momentum is confirmed by a 3.5% session gain and 13% three-session advance after adjusted EPS rose 30% and gross margin expanded 320 basis points; weak organic sales, 5.1× net leverage and cautious FY2027 sales guidance temper the setup.

sector_notes: Energy (XLE +1.85% over November 10–17) and oil services (XOP +1.19%) showed the strongest relative resilience, while consumer staples edged up 0.47%; energy ETFs nevertheless pulled back on November 17. Technology and semiconductors weakened (XLK -3.34%, SOXX -3.50%, SMH -4.87%), as did small caps (IWM -4.11%) and materials/miners (XME -7.67%, GDX -8.0%). November 17 breadth was poor, with 2,651 decliners versus 766 advancers among 3,470 liquid stocks, favoring selective post-earnings setups rather than broad momentum exposure.
